summary.headline: Week behind target on both orders and revenue, and the year stands at 94.1% of target with the required run-rate well above recent pace.

points.what: Orders came in at 834, 93.5% of the weekly target, and revenue at $58,718, 88.7% of target.
points.so_what: Both headline KPIs missed the week, so the quarter's small surplus was not extended.

points.what: Revenue fell 13.1% week on week, a change the brief marks as notable.
points.so_what: This drop is larger than normal week-to-week movement and should not be read as ordinary fluctuation.

points.what: Orders were up 58.3% and revenue up 53.8% on last year, both below the 75% growth the targets assume.
points.so_what: Growth is real but not fast enough to close the gap the targets are built on.

points.what: The cancellation rate rose for a third consecutive week, from 13.6% to 15.3%.
points.so_what: The trend is not reversing, and each percentage point of cancellations is worth $694 of revenue.

points.what: The cancellation rate has moved in the bad direction for three straight weeks and now sits at 15.3%.
points.so_what: A three-week run means this is a trend rather than noise, and it holds back revenue at $694 per percentage point.

points.what: YTD revenue is $902,394 against $959,046 of target, 94.1% attainment, with a gap of $56,652.
points.so_what: The year is behind and the shortfall has to be recovered on top of every remaining weekly target.

points.what: Hitting the full-year target of $3,888,802 requires $80,714 a week, against a recent 8-week run-rate of $60,886.
points.so_what: The required pace sits far above where the business is running, so the full-year target is out of reach at this pace.

points.what: Orders reached 93.5% of the weekly target, short by 58 orders, and revenue reached 88.7%, short by $7,517.
points.so_what: The week added to the year-to-date shortfall rather than reducing it.

points.what: QTD revenue is $186,837 against $184,491 of target, 101.3% attainment, with $697,249 still to go over 10 remaining weeks.
points.so_what: The quarter is ahead only by a thin margin, so repeat weeks like this one would tip it behind.

points.what: Jan, Feb and Mar all closed behind target, with April to date the only month ahead.
points.so_what: The year-to-date gap of $56,652 comes from the first quarter and has not yet been worked down.

points.what: LATAM orders fell 40.8% to 90, a contribution of -62 orders and 112.7% of the total week-on-week change.
points.so_what: LATAM accounts for more than the entire decline, so gains elsewhere were not enough to offset it.

points.what: EMEA orders fell 14.6% to 146, contributing -25 orders, while APAC added 27 and North America 5.
points.so_what: The two growing regions together did not cover the EMEA and LATAM losses.

points.what: Search, at 70.5% of orders, was down 3.3% to 588 and contributed -20 orders, the largest traffic-source contribution to the decline.
points.so_what: The biggest source moved down only modestly, so the order decline is spread across sources rather than concentrated in one.

points.what: AOV was $83.17, down 7.1% week on week and down 4.2% on last year.
points.so_what: Revenue fell faster than orders because each order carried less value.

points.what: The cancellation rate was 15.3%, up 0.2 pp on the week but down 1.2 pp on last year.
points.so_what: The year-on-year position is better even though the recent direction is unfavourable.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 30 Mar 2026 was 9.9%, down 1.6 pp week on week and down 1.5 pp on last year, a notable move.
points.so_what: Order quality improved on this measure, the one favourable signal among the quality KPIs.

points.what: New signups were 246, down 2.0% on the week and down 2.4% on last year, while orders were up 58.3% on last year.
points.so_what: Order growth is not being matched by growth in new accounts.

checks.name: 14-Day Return Rate names its mature week
anomaly flag acknowledged in the summary
sentences at most 30 words and 4 numbers
each slot only covers its allowed KPIs
